issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method signature differs between the problem/template and the solution. The problem statement and template expect messageOnRide() with no parameters (as shown in the UML and used in the template Main), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements it accordingly in Pig and Seal. This parameter mismatch will confuse students about the correct method signature and return format, and will prevent code that follows the problem/template (and likely the tests) from compiling against the solution interfaces.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and all implementations use the parameterless signature messageOnRide():String to match the UML and template usage, and have implementations return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to specify messageOnRide(String equipment) everywhere (and update examples and tests) so all artifacts consistently require the equipment parameter.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument Rideable.messageOnRide() method (signature: messageOnRide():String), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements it with the additional parameter in Pig and Seal. This API mismatch prevents a direct mapping from the exercise description and template usage (which call r.messageOnRide() with no arguments) to the solution code, causing compilation errors and confusion for students about the correct method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent with the problem and template by changing the interface method to messageOnRide():String (no parameters) in Rideable.java, and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() accordingly. Alternatively, if the equipment parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement and template Main usage to require and demonstrate messageOnRide(String equipment) so all artifacts share the same signature.
